# Prompt layer snapshots

Frozen, byte-exact renderings of `backend/app/services/prompts.py`, used by
`backend/tests/test_prompt_layers.py` to prove the L0/L1/L2 prompt-layering
refactor (`backend/app/services/prompt_layers.py`) is zero-behavior-change.

## Baseline

Generated by `scripts/generate_prompt_layer_snapshots.py` against
`backend/app/services/prompts.py` as it stood at commit `319f7aad` — before
any `fragment_text(...)` splicing existed. Every `<case>.txt` file here is
exactly what that commit's `prompts.py` produced for that case, with no
manual edits afterward.

## On-disk contract

- **Byte-exact.** Each file's content is the literal return value of the
  corresponding prompt function call, written with `Path.write_text(text,
  encoding="utf-8")` — no reformatting, no re-indentation, nothing added.
- **No appended trailing newline.** The file ends exactly where the
  rendered prompt string ends. If a case's own rendering ends in `\n` (most
  do, since most prompt functions end their return value with a schema-hint
  line that itself carries no trailing `\n`, or with one that does), that is
  the prompt's own content — this generator does not add or strip one.
- **One file per case**, named `<case>.txt`, where `<case>` is the key in
  `_cases()` inside the generator script.

## How to re-verify (not regenerate)

```
python3 -m pytest backend/tests/test_prompt_layers.py -q
```

This re-renders every case against the CURRENT `prompts.py` and asserts
byte-for-byte equality against the files here. A failure means the
refactor changed rendered output — fix the code, not the fixture.

## How to regenerate (only when deliberately changing prompt text)

Do **not** run the generator to "fix" a failing byte-equivalence test — that
turns the acceptance criterion into a tautology. Regenerate only when a
change to prompt text is intentional, as part of that same change's diff:

```
python3 scripts/generate_prompt_layer_snapshots.py
```

## Retirement

This fixture set is scoped to the L0/L1/L2 layering refactor, not
permanent — see the generator script's own docstring ("RETIREMENT") for the
exact rule, which mirrors the precedent already recorded in
`docs/development.md` for `ReasoningRetriever.run`'s retired refactor-only
golden snapshot. In short: the first deliberate prompt-text change after
this refactor lands must either regenerate every affected fixture here (and
say so in its PR), or retire this whole directory and the corresponding
section of `test_prompt_layers.py` (and say so in its PR) — never leave it
silently stale next to a real behavior change.
